design_rationale:
WORKLOG / TEST DOSSIER - task 1 (non-workflow payoff tree)

[1] Why this is a good test. Renee Vasquez asks only to pay her car loan off today from her checking. The payoff amount (principal + accrued interest + fees due) is scored, and the fees in it are wrong: when she opened a new Interest Checking in June and closed her Everyday Checking on 2026-06-26, her autopay stayed pointed at the closed account; PCB presented the July installment there on 2026-07-15, it came back (reversal 2026-07-16), a 25.00 returned payment fee followed and, after the 15 NC grace days, a 22.28 late charge on 2026-07-31. The payoff rule says both kinds of fee must be waived for bank error before the payoff amount is fixed, and the two waiver rules say when: the debit was an autopay debit drawn on an account whose checking record shows it closed before the debit date. The agent has to find this by reading the ledger (which fee, which returned payment, which paying account and date) against the checking records, while excluding look-alike rows: a March 2025 returned autopay debit, its 25.00 fee and a 22.28 late charge that were legitimate (Everyday was open then) and were paid by phone on 2025-04-02. Then it reconciles principal (28650.00 disbursement less 23 principal portions plus 2 reversals) and 56 days of interest, because the July return pushed last_payment_date back to 2026-06-15.

[2] Scope snapshot. Occupied by task 0: auto_ext_catchup_installment_payment, auto_ext_autopay_cancel_rate, auto_ext_autopay_enroll_rate, the workflow auto_wf_autopay_source_change and the tools post_installment_payment_660c6229, change_due_day_df9bec35, cancel_autopay_a2c51ad3, enroll_autopay_b9bffdb4. Claimed here (disjoint): auto_ext_closed_source_returned_fee_waiver, auto_ext_closed_source_late_charge_waiver, auto_ext_payoff_settlement with tools waive_returned_payment_fee_ab31cb83, waive_late_charge_e8055e73, post_payoff_payment_63569e96; workflows []. This is the last task: the union of the two scopes covers all 6 extended policies and all 7 task tools; nothing is reserved.

[3] Policies. Both waivers: trigger state_due (a fee assessed contrary to the charter is owed back whether or not anyone calls), subject auto_fee_waiver, base_policy_refs [auto_evt_fee_waiver] (the only base policy on that event), overwrite [] - they refine base 'A bank_error waiver applies to any fee assessed contrary to this charter ... it has no limit' and 'A fee is waived in full, never in part' with a concrete, checkable ground stated in the extended rules themselves: 'PCB keeps an autopay enrollment drawing only on a source account that is open on each debit date', which extends to every debit base auto_evt_autopay's enrollment-time requirement ('The autopay source must be a checking account of the same customer in active status when autopay is enrolled'); a debit PCB presents to an account its records show closed before the debit date is therefore PCB's error. Base names no such ground itself; the base bank_error list is open ('such as'), and no base sentence forbids the waiver, so this is additive and overwrite stays []. Cross-category numeric read: CFIELD checking closed_date of the debit's paying account (dynamic filter checking_account_id = the payment's counterparty_account_id). Payoff: on_request, subject auto_payment, refs [auto_evt_payment_allocation, auto_evt_payoff_and_lien], overwrite [] - payoff = principal + accrued interest + fees due as in base, with ledger-reconciled principal and fees, the prepayment-penalty clause kept (0.00), and a posted-funds branch reading CFIELD ledger_balance of the active checking account.

[4] Base-invariant card. auto_fee_waiver (steps 6 and 8): courtesy_count 'The customer's courtesy late charge waivers in the rolling 365 days ... must be below late_charge_courtesy_waivers_365d.' - no courtesy waiver exists on any of her loans (0 < 1); on_time_before 'The installments immediately before the late one must show at least late_charge_courtesy_min_on_time consecutive on-time installments' - January to June 2026 were all credited by autopay within grace (6); loan_open_for_courtesy - status active; waive_once - no auto_fee_waiver names either fee. auto_payment (step 10): loan_open - status active; auto_evt_payoff_and_lien has no gate on auto_payment (policy_scope). No time gates are involved (the lien release deadline applies to auto_release_lien, not written here).

[5] Business-object card. Target loan: New Vehicle Loan (last4 9147). Fee 1: returned_payment fee 702892f0-... (2026-07-16, source_item_id = July debit 44b9f007-...). Fee 2: late_charge 2b892ebc-... (2026-07-31, installment 2026-07-15). The July debit's counterparty is the Everyday account 534d0f08-... closed 2026-06-26. Excluded look-alikes: the 2025-03-18 returned payment fee and the 2025-03-31 late charge (the March 2025 debit was presented while Everyday was open; both fees were settled by the 2025-04-02 phone payment's 47.28 fees portion) - the policies take the most recent fee of each kind, and even if tested these fail the closed-before-debit test. Each waiver carries its fee id as source_item_id; the payoff carries no installment and the Interest Checking ending 9372 as counterparty.

[6] initial_state rows. customers (NC, credentials). checking_accounts: Everyday (closed 2026-06-26) - removing it or its closed_date makes both waivers 0 and the payoff 19825.69; Interest Checking (active, 24918.40) - the paying account; removing it gives funds 0 and a payoff amount of 0.00 (no payoff). auto_loans row. auto_transactions (31 rows): disbursement, 20 on-time autopay payments (principal reconciliation and the on-time streak), March 2025 returned debit + reversal + fee + late charge + phone payment + settlement (distractors that teach the charter correctly: a late charge after grace, fees paid first), July 2026 returned debit + reversal + fee + late charge (the load-bearing error). Automatic clauses: August installment not yet due (2026-08-15); 26 days past due < 30 so still active; no GAP (so no GAP refund is lit by the payoff); the lien release after the payoff is due within 10 business days and is not an obligation at frozen_time. No cache trap: fees_due 47.28 and principal_balance 19590.85 equal the ledger.

[7] Problem-tree card. Root auto_ext_payoff_settlement. Edge A -> auto_ext_closed_source_returned_fee_waiver: value_input on binding fees_due; condition 'Every returned payment fee that followed an autopay debit presented to a closed source account has been waived before the payoff amount is fixed.'; policy_source 'Before the payoff amount is fixed, every returned payment fee that followed an autopay debit presented to a closed source account is waived for bank error under its own rule.'; resolved_by waive_returned_payment_fee_ab31cb83; false at frozen_time: fee row 702892f0 amount 25.00, July debit counterparty = Everyday, Everyday closed_date 2026-06-26, fees_due 47.28. Edge B -> auto_ext_closed_source_late_charge_waiver: value_input on fees_due; condition 'Every late charge on an installment left unpaid by an autopay debit presented to a closed source account has been waived before the payoff amount is fixed.'; resolved_by waive_late_charge_e8055e73; false: late charge 2b892ebc 22.28 unwaived. Topological order: returned-fee waiver, late-charge waiver, payoff. Parallel edges are order-free: calc_t1.py 'LC-first payoff 19778.41' equals gold. Deletion sensitivity: skip A -> 19803.41; skip B -> 19800.69; skip both -> 19825.69 (gold 19778.41). user_scenario never mentions a fee, a waiver or the July debit; tools check nothing.

[8] Persona design. Renee Vasquez, organized, slightly anxious pharmacist on a lunch break; opens with the surface goal only; phone, DOB, SSN last four (ZIP if needed), the Interest Checking ending 9372 and loan last4 9147 are given when asked; she explains the old Everyday was closed in late June only if asked why she is not using it. Passive reactions: surprise if told a July payment failed (she assumed autopay moved over); thanks the agent if told bank-error charges are being removed, without ever asking for removal; accepts the payoff figure the agent states without a figure of her own; ends once the payoff is confirmed (the last gold action). She asks for nothing beyond that (no title or lien question). Gold answers 25.00, 22.28, 19778.41 do not appear in the persona.

[9] Traps. (a) Paying off with the fees included (19825.69) - the payoff rule requires the waivers first. (b) Waiving the March 2025 fees too, or treating them as the target - they were legitimate and paid. (c) Treating the late charge as a courtesy case (a courtesy waiver would use the borrower's allowance and is a different ground; the late charge is a bank error here). (d) Using the recorded 6.24 rate with interest from 2026-07-15 (the returned debit) instead of last_payment_date 2026-06-15. (e) Drawing on the closed Everyday account. (f) Posting a scheduled catch-up payment instead of a payoff.

[10] Standard solution. find_customers(7045550193) -> verify(phone, 1976-11-08, 9261) -> find_auto_loans -> find_auto_transactions -> find_checking_accounts -> waive returned payment fee 702892f0 for 25.00 (0.00 to principal) -> waive late charge 2b892ebc for 22.28 (0.00 to principal) -> payoff 19778.41 = 0.00 fees + 187.56 interest + 19590.85 principal from the Interest Checking ending 9372.

[11] Verification and gate runs. calc_t1.py (replays gold writes with the real tools, evaluates each compute on the handling-time world): WRP {fee_id 702892f0, channel autopay_pcb, debit_date 2026-07-15, source_closed 2026-06-26, pcb_error True, fee_amount 25.0, prior_waivers 0, result 25.0}; WLC {charge_installment 2026-07-15, reversals 1, pcb_error True, charge_amount 22.28, result 22.28}; PAYOFF {principal 19590.85, fees_due 0.0, days 56, accrued 187.56, penalty 0, payoff 19778.41, funds 24918.4, result 19778.41}; skip {6} 19803.41; skip {8} 19800.69; skip {6,8} 19825.69; LC-first 19778.41. In task 0's world the same two waiver computes return 0 (pcb_error False: that account closed 2026-08-10, after the 2026-08-05 debit), so they impose no obligation there. Per-task gates (--task 1): EXTENDED OK; TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK; REPLAY OK (11 acts, closure 35 = init 35); SOLVABILITY OK; COMPUTE OK (3 comps, 29 factors, 40 history rows, 9 branches); GROUNDING OK; SCOPE OK.

[12] Closure. computations policy set = charter_scope.extended_policies = required_documents (same order) = {returned-fee waiver, late-charge waiver, payoff}; task_tools = the three tools in first-call order; no workflow tool is used. Rule/compute two-way sweep: every binding carries a rule quotation in compute_basis; every rule quantity (most recent fee of each kind, its payment by source_item_id or installment, reversal test, closed-before-debit comparison, full amount, once-only, ledger principal, ledger fees, day count exclusive/inclusive, single rounding, penalty only above zero, posted-funds branch, portions equal to the parts) has a binding; applied_to_principal is fixed by 'Of the waived amount, the part already paid from a payment is applied to principal on the waiver date and the rest reduces fees due'.

[13] Draft recomputation from visible context only: the lookups show the July autopay debit drawn on account ...8843 whose record says closed 2026-06-26, a 25.00 returned payment fee and a 22.28 late charge after it; the published waiver rules make both bank errors; the payoff rule requires them waived first; payoff = 19590.85 + (19590.85 x 6.24% / 365 x 56 = 187.56) + 0.00 = 19778.41 from the only active account. Agrees with gold.

[14] Difficulty-level closing record. Two tasks, one workflow (task 0), 6 extended policies each claimed exactly once, 7 tools each called by exactly one task; every policy reads checking numerically (ledger_balance or closed_date/opened_date) and the read changes its result in its own task's world. Revisions: (r1) the old account's closed date in task 1 was set before the July due date (2026-06-26) and, in task 0, after the August debit (2026-08-10), so each bank-error rule fires only where intended.

[15] Round-2 note (audit revision 1 verdict PASS, no change to any value or action). OB-T1-1 / O9: both waiver rules now state the closed-source premise as their own sentence ('PCB keeps an autopay enrollment drawing only on a source account that is open on each debit date ...') instead of attributing it to base, and [3] above no longer says base auto_evt_autopay states it. O5: the payoff rule's 'Before the payoff amount is fixed, every returned payment fee that followed an autopay debit presented to a closed source account is waived' (and its late-charge twin) and the waiver rules' 'The fee considered is the most recent returned_payment fee on the loan' / 'The late charge considered is the most recent late_charge fee on the loan' coincide in this world because exactly one qualifying fee of each kind exists (the 2025 pair fails the closed-before-debit test and is settled); documented as a limit of the waiver computes. O2, O3, O4, O6, O11: no effect here (credit date before cutoff on a business day, one active account, no half-cent tie, funds cover the payoff, no later read of the checking balance). Re-run values: 25.00 / 22.28 / 19778.41, unchanged.
user_scenario:
You are Renee Vasquez, 49, a hospital pharmacist in Charlotte, North Carolina, calling on your Monday lunch break. You are organized and a little anxious, you like to hear things once and clearly, and you keep your answers short. You are selling your Tesla Model 3 this week, the buyer's check has already cleared into your PCB checking account, and you want to pay off your car loan with PCB today, in full, straight from that checking account. You start with exactly that: you want to pay off your car loan today from your checking account.
You do not volunteer your details. When the agent asks for them, you give your mobile number, 7045550193, then your date of birth, November 8, 1976 (1976-11-08), and the last four of your Social Security number, 9261; if one more thing is needed, your ZIP code is 28205. The loan is your only car loan with PCB and you remember its number ends in 9147. The money should come from your Interest Checking account ending in 9372, which you opened in June; you closed your old Everyday Checking in late June, and if the agent asks why you are not using it you tell them so.
If the agent mentions that a July payment on the loan did not go through, you are surprised: you had assumed the automatic payment moved over when you opened the new account, and you say that. If the agent tells you some charges on the loan are being taken off because they were the bank's mistake, you say thank you and let them go ahead; you never ask for any charge to be removed yourself and you do not know which charges there are. You are happy for the agent to do everything on your behalf. When the agent tells you the payoff amount, you do not check it against any figure of your own; you tell them to go ahead and take exactly that amount from the Interest Checking ending in 9372 today. Once the agent confirms the loan is paid off, you thank them and end the call.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The two waivers are parallel prerequisites of the payoff. Each names a different fee, writes its own waiver row (id built from its own arguments) and lowers fees_due by its own amount; neither compute reads the other's row (each counts only waivers naming its own fee). Actual run (calc_t1.py): with the late charge waived first the payoff recomputes to 19778.41, the same as the gold order, and the terminal rows are identical because the tools write the same rows and the same final fees_due 0.00.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the returned-fee waiver leaves fees due 25.00 and the payoff recomputes to 19803.41 instead of 19778.41 (fees_portion 25.00 instead of 0.00); the waiver row is missing from the terminal.
Skipping the late-charge waiver leaves fees due 22.28 and the payoff recomputes to 19800.69 instead of 19778.41; skipping both gives 19825.69.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario asks only to pay the loan off today from her checking; she never asks for any charge to be removed and does not know which charges exist. The July payment and the bank-error removal appear only as reactions after the agent raises them ('If the agent mentions ...', 'If the agent tells you some charges ... are being taken off').
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: post_payoff_payment_63569e96 creates the payoff entry and sets the loan to paid_off with whatever amount and portions it is given, without reading fees_due or any waiver; the two waiver tools write their row and reduce fees_due by their arguments without checking fee type, closure dates or earlier waivers. An agent that skips a waiver gets a normal payoff receipt and only the terminal amounts differ.
